# Owl of Access Requests (`owl-of-access-requests`)

Tracks patient right-of-access requests against the HIPAA clock (30 days plus one 30-day extension with written notice, or your shorter state limit): requests past due or due soon, answered late, extensions with no timely notice, denials with no reason and fees above your fee settings. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Owl never sends records to anyone; your release-of-information staff do. Owl never issues refunds.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y owl-of-access-requests demo
npx -y owl-of-access-requests mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice) and made-up patients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`access-requests.csv`](fixtures/access-requests.csv): Planted: a request answered in 11 days (AR-1001, clean), paper copies sent 8 days late and charged 25.00 against an allowed 15.00 (AR-1002), an open request 15 days past due (AR-1003), an extension whose notice went out after the first 30 days and 10 paper pages charged 8.00 against an allowed 7.50 (AR-1004), a request due within 7 days (AR-1005), a denial with no reason or date recorded (AR-1006), an email copy charged 15.00 against the 6.50 flat fee (AR-1007) and a new request not due yet (AR-1008).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 30 days plus one 30-day extension, a 6.50 flat fee for electronic copies, paper at 5.00 plus 0.25 a page, capped at 50. These are examples; use your policy and state law. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `owl_check` | List access requests that are late, due soon, extended without notice, denied without a reason or overcharged. | runs |
| `owl_write_report` | Write owl-access-requests.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and owl-access-requests.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/owl). | runs |
| `owl_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `owl_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `owl_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `owl_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `records_release` | Owl never sends records to anyone; your release-of-information staff do. | refused |
| `refund_issue` | Owl never issues refunds. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `owl_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `requests` (required) | Access request log under --root: request, patient, received date, requester type, format, pages, extension, notice date, fulfilled or denied date, reason and fee |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: response_days, extension_days, warn_days, flat_fee, per_page, base_fee, fee_cap |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx owl-of-access-requests inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Access request log (`requests`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | text | Request ID, Request #, Request, ROI #, Log #, Ticket |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `received` (required) | date | Received, Date Received, Received On, Request Date, Requested |
| `requester_type` | text | Requester Type, Requested By, Requester, Request Type |
| `format` | text | Format, Delivery, Media, Copy Format, Delivery Method |
| `pages` | number | Pages, Page Count, # Pages |
| `extended` | text | Extended, Extension, Extension Taken |
| `extension_notice_on` | date | Extension Notice, Extension Notice Date, Extension Letter Sent |
| `fulfilled` | date | Fulfilled, Completed, Sent, Date Sent, Closed, Released, Date Completed |
| `denied` | text | Denied, Denial |
| `denied_on` | date | Denied On, Denial Date |
| `denial_reason` | text | Denial Reason, Reason Denied, Reason |
| `fee` | amount | Fee, Fee Charged, Charge, Amount Charged |
| `postage` | amount | Postage, Shipping |

## Settings file (`owl_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `response_days` | Calendar days to answer (HIPAA: 30; some states are shorter) |
| `extension_days` | Days one extension adds (HIPAA: 30) |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn; default 7 |
| `flat_fee` | Flat fee you charge for electronic copies (HHS describes $6.50 as an option), or null |
| `per_page` | Per-page fee for paper copies under your policy or state law, or null |
| `base_fee` | Fixed fee added to per-page fees (labor or search fee your state allows), default 0 |
| `fee_cap` | Most you charge for one request, or null |

## Memory

`owl_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `owl_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "owl-of-access-requests": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "owl-of-access-requests",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add owl-of-access-requests -- npx -y owl-of-access-requests mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
owl-of-access-requests tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
owl-of-access-requests sources               # the columns each input is read from
owl-of-access-requests inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
owl-of-access-requests call owl_check '{"requests":"<requests>"}'
owl-of-access-requests eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
owl-of-access-requests demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
